text: Chapter 2 starts here — what is Delta Lake, actually?

Foundations Lesson 42 covered why Parquet is the analytics default. Delta Lake starts from exactly that — every Delta table's actual data files are Parquet files, unchanged. Delta doesn't replace Parquet, it wraps it.

Here's the real problem it solves: writing a batch of Parquet files isn't atomic. If a write job fails halfway through, you can be left with a partial set of files, and no record of which set is the real, complete version. Foundations never had to worry about this, because every write there ran once, uninterrupted.

What Delta adds is a folder called underscore delta underscore log — a sequential, append-only record of every change ever made. This one log is the actual mechanism behind everything else this chapter covers: atomic writes, time travel, safe concurrent updates.
Same Parquet files, plus a log that makes them trustworthy — that's why Delta is the real-world default now, not the exception. Next lesson: Delta tables versus Parquet tables, made concrete.
